Alex — great to meet you and Priya. Confirmed we got the CSV (thanks). Below is our proposed POC plan and a concrete capacity recommendation so you can sign off fast. High-level summary, then explicit next steps / owners.

POC goals / success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 200ms for standard question path (avg sequence length ~128 tokens).
- Throughput & stability: sustain 60 concurrent requests (avg concurrency window) with no more than 2% 500-level errors during a 1-hour soak.
- Quality: embedding-based retrieval trip test: mean cosine similarity improvement of >= 0.10 over baseline (your existing vector store), and retrieval precision @10 >= 0.88 on the eval set you provided.
- Operational: rollout test for graceful fallback to smaller model under constrained capacity with <1% user-visible failures.

Capacity recommendation for the POC (timeline: 2 weeks setup, 2 weeks evaluation)
- Reserved capacity (baseline): 2 x NVIDIA A100-equivalent (or 4 x T4-equivalent) nodes dedicated for the trial. This gives predictable latency for the steady-state traffic.
- Autoscale policy (for bursts): min_instances=2 (reserved), scale_up_steps: +2 at 60% CPU/GPU util sustained for 90s, +2 further at 85% util up to max_instances=8. Burst behavior supports short spikes up to 3x steady-state for 30 minutes; for sustained higher load we recommend adding reserved capacity.
- Burst expectations: brief spikes (5–30 minutes) to ~180 req/s handled by autoscale; sustained >30 minutes at that level will be throttled or moved to queued processing unless you authorize additional reserved nodes.

Operational notes
- KV-cache warmup: we’ll recommend a warmup run at start to pre-populate prefixes for your 10 most common flows (Priyom will coordinate).
- Data handling: we’ll set up a customer VPC link and ephemeral staging tokens for redacted PHI tests. No PHI will be stored outside your workspace without explicit config.

- Infra / runtime lead: Marcus Lin — instance sizing, autoscale policy, cost estimate
- Customer success: Evelyn Hart — success criteria validation and go/no-go decision

Quick technical notes from infra:
- The 2 x A100-equivalent baseline is reasonable for the 60 concurrent target if your sequence lengths average ~128 and KV cache reuse is high. If your eval set shows longer sequences (>=256) or lots of long-context retrievals we should bump to 3 reserved nodes.
- Memory footprint: factor in ~24GB GPU memory per concurrent heavy session; we’ll instrument GPU utilization during the first warmup run and provide a recommended cap.
- Autoscale considerations: to avoid cold-start latency for short bursts we’ll keep one warm spare (GPU with warmed KV cache) during business hours. That increases baseline cost slightly but keeps 95th latency lower.
- Cost pick: we can provide two pricing options in the MOA — Reserved-heavy (lower unit cost, higher commit) vs Flexible (lower commit, slightly higher unit cost for burst).

I’ll draft a short infra checklist for Priyom to run during the kickoff: VPC peering, sample keys, pre-warm job, EV/QA endpoint for your engineers.

—Marcus
